cells.quote: For more than a decade NAEP data have consistently demonstrated that more than half of black fourth graders perform below the NAEP Basic level in reading compared to about 20% of white students
cells.note: This is a comparison from repeated NAEP reports, not a new experiment; the study text does not report a printed effect size.

cells.quote: Of these 92 students, 57 (62%) had a pro ﬁle consistent with dyslexia, and 53 of the 57 (93%) were African-American; 7 (8%) students did not have dyslexia, 7 (8%) students spoke Spanish as their primary language and 21 (23%) students were classiﬁed in the indeterminate category.
cells.note: The study reports group counts but no statistical test or uncertainty estimate for the racial-group comparison.

D.treatment: Students below the NAEP Basic level

O.outcome_detail: oral reading fluency and foundational reading skills

cells.quote: Their data indicated that “signiﬁcant percentages of the students who perform below the NAEP Basic level on the 4 th grade NAEP reading assessment have poor oral reading ﬂuency and foundational skills. ”
cells.note: This finding is reported by Cassidy et al. from White and associates' examination of a nationally representative sample; the study text does not provide the comparison percentage or effect size.
